title: Teach Extraction Output
description: The only shape the language model step of POST /teach/parse may return (ADR 0008). Every free-text field refuses markup (< and >), C0 and C1 control characters, DEL, U+00A0, the bidirectional controls (U+061C, U+200E, U+200F, U+202A to U+202E, U+2066 to U+2069), the zero-width characters U+200B to U+200D, U+2028, U+2029 and U+FEFF. The API validates every answer against this schema, normalises each action (NFKC, whitespace runs collapsed to one space, trimmed, lower-cased - the same normalisation the relation endpoints apply) and then checks that every cited candidate was in the list it sent, that no intent joins a concept to itself, that no normalised rel action is is a or equivalent to, and that every spec intent has a draftable form (ADR 0008). Any failure makes the whole answer invalid: no model draft is returned and the sentence is listed in unresolved. The API turns valid intents into drafts with the same mapping as the rule-based grammar; the model never writes and never produces a draft directly.

kind.description: rel: subject action object. spec: subject is a kind of object (subject is the specialised child, object the parent), like the grammar's spec intent.

action.description: Required for rel, absent for spec. Lower-case present-tense verb phrase read subject to object, for example sells or focuses on; a canonical predicate of the reference lexicon when one has the same meaning. No leading or trailing space. After normalisation, is a and equivalent to are refused for rel.

rule.description: spec only: the condition that defines the child, as in a machine that has run 5,000 hours.

domainKey.description: The domain template the new concept belongs to, or null to inherit from its parent. A domain prefix typed in the sentence always wins.

explanation.description: Plain text, no markup: why this intent, for example which earlier concept a back-reference points to.

span.description: The part of the sentence this intent comes from. Used to order intents and to build unresolved text; never returned as is.

conceptRef.description: An existing concept cited by the handle the API sent in the candidate list (c0 is always the company root), or a new concept by label. A new label that matches an existing concept of the company (case-insensitive, singular or plural) is resolved to that concept by the API, as the grammar does.

newLabel.description: No leading or trailing space, so a whitespace-only label is refused.

text.description: Located in the sentence the API holds; the response carries the matching substring of that sentence, never this text.
